claim: The existence of local structural frustration for F70 results in increased dynamics for both F70 and Y71, which leads to occasional loop opening in nDsbDox.

claim: Following opening of the cap loop at 82.5 ns, Y70 and Y71 continue to sample a variety of conformations, which could be important for the cap loop to access a fully open structure.
source: Following opening of the cap loop at 82.5 ns, Y70 and Y71 continue to sample a variety of conformations, which could be important for the cap loop to access a fully open structure.

claim: The loop is often prevented from closing fully by the side chain of Y71 which sits in between C109 and F70 in a 'blocking' conformation.
source: Interestingly, as the F70-to-C109 distance decreases, the loop is often prevented from closing fully by the side chain of Y71 which sits in between C109 and F70 in a 'blocking' conformation (for example at 93.2 ns and later at 151.9 and 155.8 ns [Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 5]).

source: The cap loop can also adopt conformations that are more open than the open 1VRS structure (at ~145 and~181 ns); these structures are characterized by larger F70-C109 and Y71-C109 distances (>16 Å and 10 Å, respectively) (Figure 5—figure supplements 2, 5).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and illustrated in supplementary figures showing very open conformations.

claim: Very open conformations of the cap loop may be important for the initial docking of cDsbD prior to nDsbD/cDsbD complex formation, as they would minimize the steric clashes between the two domains during binding.
source: These conformations may be important for the initial docking of cDsbD prior to nDsbD/cDsbD complex formation, as they would minimize the steric clashes between the two domains during binding.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a speculation about the functional importance of very open conformations.

claim: The backbone ϕ and ψ torsion angles of D68, E69, F70, Y71 and G72 show clear changes at 82.5 ns when the loop begins to open.
source: The backbone ϕ and ψ torsion angles of D68, E69, F70, Y71 and G72 also show clear changes at 82.5 ns when the loop begins to open (Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 4).

source: E69 ϕ and ψ become less variable in the open loop while the ϕ and ψ values for D68 and F70 become more variable.

claim: The torsion angle changes are correlated with loss of the hydrogen bond between the amide nitrogen of Y71 and the side chain carboxyl group of D68 upon loop opening.
source: These torsion angle changes are correlated with loss of the hydrogen bond between the amide nitrogen of Y71 and the side chain carboxyl group of D68 upon loop opening.

evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on hydrogen bond analysis from MD simulations.

claim: During simulations of loop closing, Y71 adopts conformations in which it sits between F70 and C109 thus blocking complete closure of the loop.
source: We have also investigated the dynamics of Y71 in the simulations of loop closing, and in particular those simulations in which the loop fails to close completely within 10 ns. During these trajectories Y71 adopts conformations in which it sits between F70 and C109 thus blocking complete closure of the loop as observed, for example, at 93.2 ns in the major opening event and at 2.8 ns in the incomplete loop closing seen in Figure 3G (Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and illustrated in figures showing the blocking conformation.

claim: The cap-loop motif is more conserved than the flanking β-strands.
source: We find that the cap-loop motif is more conserved than the flanking β-strands, in agreement with the central role that this structural motif plays in nDsbD function.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on bioinformatics sequence analysis.

claim: In 53% of the sequences an F or a Y is found at position 70.
source: In 53% of the sequences an F or a Y is found at position 70; in a further 36.4% of the sequences a residue with a relatively bulky side chain (K/I/L/E/V/T/N), which would shield the cysteines from solvent, is found at position 70.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on sequence alignment analysis.

claim: In 85% of sequences an F or a Y is found at position 71.
source: Interestingly, in 85% of sequences an F or a Y is found at position 71; in a further 5.2% of the sequences position 71 is occupied by a bulky hydrophobic residue (I or L).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on sequence alignment analysis.

claim: The high conservation of an aromatic amino acid at position 71 highlights the key role played by Y71 in contributing to loop opening and in preventing rapid loop closure.
source: This high conservation of an aromatic amino acid observed for this position further highlights the key role played by Y71 in contributing to loop opening and, more importantly, in preventing rapid loop closure, thus likely facilitating the interaction of nDsbD with cDsbD prior to reductant transfer.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as an interpretation of the sequence conservation data.

claim: For nDsbDred, no evidence for μs-ms dynamics in the cap loop or the active site were found using 15N NMR relaxation dispersion experiments.
source: For nDsbDred, no evidence for μs-ms dynamics in the cap loop or the active site were found (Figure 6A–C).

source: This observation is consistent with the absence of a significantly populated open state of nDsbDred.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as an interpretation of the relaxation dispersion data.

claim: In nDsbDox, eight residues (V64, W65, E69, F70, Y71, G72, K73 and S74), all in the cap-loop region, showed strong relaxation dispersion effects.
source: By contrast, in nDsbDox, eight residues, V64, W65, E69, F70, Y71, G72, K73 and S74, all in the cap-loop region, showed strong relaxation dispersion effects (Figures 6D–F and 7A).

claim: The peaks of C103, C109 and Y110 are not visible and the peak of A104 is very weak in the spectrum of nDsbDox, but not nDsbDred, likely due to extensive chemical exchange processes in nDsbDox leading to 1HN and/or 15N peak broadening.
source: These results are consistent with previous observations about peak intensities in 1H-15N HSQC spectra (Mavridou et al., 2012). The peaks of C103, C109 and Y110 are not visible and the peak of A104 is very weak in the spectrum of nDsbDox, but not nDsbDred (Mavridou et al., 2012), likely due to extensive chemical exchange processes in nDsbDox leading to 1HN and/or 15N peak broadening.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on NMR spectral observations with citation to previous work.

claim: The cap loop of nDsbDox, and likely also the active-site cysteines, exchange between different conformations on the μs-ms timescale, whereas nDsbDred adopts a single conformation on this timescale.
source: Thus, the cap loop of nDsbDox, and likely also the active-site cysteines, exchange between different conformations on the μs-ms timescale, whereas nDsbDred adopts a single conformation on this timescale.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a conclusion from the relaxation dispersion experiments.

claim: Analysis of the relaxation dispersion data collected at 25°C showed that nDsbDox undergoes a single global exchange process, between a dominant major state (pA≈98%) and an alternative minor state (pB≈2%).
source: Analysis of the relaxation dispersion data collected at 25°C (using CATIA [Vallurupalli et al., 2008; Baldwin et al., 2011a; Alderson et al., 2019]) showed that nDsbDox undergoes a single global exchange process, between a dominant major state (pA98%) and an alternative minor state (pB2%) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on analysis of relaxation dispersion data using CATIA software.

claim: The relaxation dispersion data for all residues in the cap loop of nDsbDox recorded at five temperatures could be fitted simultaneously, confirming that a single process underlies the μs-ms chemical exchange.
source: The relaxation dispersion data for all residues in the cap loop recorded at the five temperatures could be fitted simultaneously (Baldwin et al., 2011a; Alderson et al., 2019; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1—source data 1). This confirmed that a single process underlies the μs-ms chemical exchange in the cap loop of nDsbDox.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by global fitting results shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The minor 'excited' state of nDsbDox is enthalpically, but not entropically, more favorable than the major ground state.
source: The minor 'excited' state is enthalpically, but not entropically, more favorable than the major ground state of nDsbDox.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on thermodynamic analysis of temperature-dependent relaxation dispersion data.

claim: The fits of temperature-dependent relaxation dispersion data demonstrated that no enthalpic barrier separates the ground and excited state of nDsbDox.
source: The fits also demonstrated that no enthalpic barrier separates the ground and excited state of nDsbDox.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on analysis of the temperature-dependent data.

claim: The absence of an enthalpic barrier between the two states might mean that no favorable interactions have to be broken in the transition state, but that the diffusion process itself may limit the speed of the transition.
source: This absence of an enthalpic barrier between the two states might mean that no favorable interactions have to be broken in the transition state, but that the diffusion process itself may limit the speed of the transition (Dill and Bromberg, 2010).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a speculation about the mechanism with citation to a reference.

claim: The conformation adopted by the cap loop in the minor state of nDsbDox might be similar to the conformation of nDsbDred.

evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by comparison shown in Figure 7B.

source: The 15N chemical shift differences between the major and minor states do, however, resemble the chemical shift differences between the oxidized and reduced isoforms of nDsbD (Figure 7C; Mavridou et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 7C showing the correlation.

claim: The differences between the chemical shifts of the minor state of nDsbDox and those of nDsbDred likely reflect the local electronic and steric differences between having a disulfide bond (in the minor state of nDsbDox) and two cysteine thiols (in nDsbDred) in the active site.
source: Nonetheless, the correlation in Figure 7C is not perfect; the differences between the chemical shifts of the minor state of nDsbDox and those of nDsbDred likely reflect the local electronic and steric differences between having a disulfide bond (in the minor state of nDsbDox) and two cysteine thiols (in nDsbDred) in the active site.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as an interpretation of the imperfect correlation.

claim: The sign of the chemical shift differences between the major and minor state, which could be determined experimentally for W65, E69, F70, Y71, G72 and K73, indicated that the minor state structure of the cap loop of nDsbDox is not disordered.
source: Importantly, the sign of the chemical shift differences between the major and minor state, which could be determined experimentally for W65, E69, F70, Y71, G72 and K73, further indicated that the minor state structure of the cap loop of nDsbDox is not disordered (Figure 7D and Figure 7—source data 1), but instead may be similar to that adopted in nDsbDred (Figure 7E and Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7D and 7E.

claim: In the alternative minor state of nDsbDox, the C103 and C109 side chains likely adopt a 'reduced-like' conformation.
source: The alternative minor state of nDsbDox, which we detected by NMR relaxation dispersion, can also be attributed to coupling between the dynamics of the active-site cysteine residues and the cap loop. In this alternative minor state, the C103 and C109 side chains likely adopt a 'reduced-like' conformation.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as an interpretation of the relaxation dispersion data.

source: Both side chains adopt a gauche- conformation (χ1 ~ −60o) in nDsbDox, but a trans conformation (χ1 ~ 180o) in nDsbDred.

source: Model building of a disulfide bond into the reduced 3PFU crystal structure followed by energy minimization with XPLOR (Brunger, 1992) showed that the resulting 'oxidized' structure maintains the 'reduced-like' trans conformation (χ1 ~ −140o) for the cysteine side chains and the gauche- conformation for F70 (Figure 8B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 8B showing the model structure.

claim: This 'reduced-like' conformation for nDsbDox, with a more tightly packed active site and a cap loop which lacks frustration, might be enthalpically more favorable and entropically less favorable than the major state of nDsbDox.
source: This 'reduced-like' conformation for nDsbDox, with a more tightly packed active site and a cap loop which lacks frustration, might be enthalpically more favorable and entropically less favorable than the major state of nDsbDox as shown by the analysis of relaxation dispersion data collected at multiple temperatures (Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a speculation supported by thermodynamic analysis.

source: Previously, NMR relaxation-dispersion experiments and MD simulations have detected complex dynamics in BPTI stemming from one of its disulfide bonds (Grey et al., 2003; Shaw et al., 2010; Xue et al., 2012), further suggesting that the disulfide bond shapes the μs-ms dynamics of the active-site and cap-loop regions of nDsbDox.

source: The X-ray structure of oxidized Δloop-nDsbD shows that deletion of the cap loop does not cause any significant changes in structure; a Cα RMSD of 0.25 Å is obtained for residues 12–122 (Figure 6—figure supplement 2 and Figure 6—figure supplement 2—source data 1).

evidence: The claim is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 6H showing the flat dispersion profile.

source: Thus, truncation of the cap loop alters the μs-ms dynamics of the cap-loop region and the active-site cysteines, further supporting our proposed model of tight coupling between the cap loop and active-site cysteines.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a conclusion from the Δloop-nDsbDox experiments.

claim: The conformational dynamics of the active-site cysteines and the cap loop are coupled and behave in an oxidation-state-dependent manner.
source: We have studied oxidized and reduced nDsbD using NMR experiments and microsecond duration MD simulations, and have demonstrated that the conformational dynamics of the active-site cysteines and the cap loop are coupled and behave in an oxidation-state-dependent manner.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a main conclusion of the study.

source: We showed that the cap loop is rigid in nDsbDred, whilst it exhibits more complex dynamics in nDsbDox (Figure 8).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 8 summarizing the dynamics.

claim: For nDsbDred we found no evidence for a significant population with an open cap loop.
source: Although the cap loop is predominately closed and ordered in both oxidation states, for nDsbDred we found no evidence for a significant population with an open cap loop.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a conclusion from NMR and MD studies.

claim: The cap loop of nDsbDred remains closed at all times, to protect the active-site cysteine thiol groups from non-cognate reactions in the oxidizing environment of the periplasm.
source: Our results argue that the cap loop of nDsbDred remains closed at all times, to protect the active-site cysteine thiol groups from non-cognate reactions in the oxidizing environment of the periplasm.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a conclusion about the functional role of the closed loop.

claim: The nDsbDred cap loop may only open to expose the cysteine thiols via an induced-fit mechanism when it encounters its legitimate binding partners, for example CcmG, DsbC and DsbG.
source: As such, the nDsbDred cap loop may only open to expose the cysteine thiols via an induced-fit mechanism when it encounters its legitimate binding partners, for example CcmG, DsbC and DsbG.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a proposed mechanism for nDsbDred.

claim: In nDsbDox, the cap loop opens spontaneously in MD simulations and while fully open conformations of the cap loop tended to close, partially open structures were stable.
source: In nDsbDox, on the other hand, the cap loop opens spontaneously in MD simulations and while fully open conformations of the cap loop tended to close, partially open structures were stable.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on MD simulation observations.

claim: nDsbDox may form a complex with its sole legitimate binding partner, cDsbDred, via a conformational selection mechanism.
source: Thus, nDsbDox may form a complex with its sole legitimate binding partner, cDsbDred, via a conformational selection mechanism.

claim: NMR relaxation dispersion experiments provided no evidence for a long-lived open or disordered conformation of the cap loop in nDsbDox.
source: Notably, NMR relaxation dispersion experiments provided no evidence for a long-lived open or disordered conformation of the cap loop as might have been expected.

claim: Local frustration in nDsbDox, but not in nDsbDred, gives rise to differences in the dynamics of the two redox isoforms, on multiple timescales.
source: Importantly, combining NMR experiments and MD simulations, we showed how local frustration (Ferreiro et al., 2007; Ferreiro et al., 2011) in nDsbDox, but not in nDsbDred, gives rise to differences in the dynamics of the two redox isoforms, on multiple timescales, providing insight into how this could affect protein function.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a main conclusion combining NMR and MD results.

claim: In nDsbDred, the cap loop packs perfectly onto the active-site cysteines and the closed conformation is stable.
source: In nDsbDred, the cap loop packs perfectly onto the active-site cysteines and the closed conformation is stable, something that is crucial in the very oxidizing environment in which the domain has to provide electrons.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a conclusion about the structural stability.

claim: In nDsbDox, the disulfide bond disrupts the tight fit of the aromatic ring of F70.
source: By contrast, in nDsbDox, the disulfide bond disrupts this tight fit of the aromatic ring of F70.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a conclusion about the structural effect of the disulfide bond.

claim: F70 is no longer locked in a single conformation in nDsbDox and switches freely between gauche- and trans orientations.
source: Consequently F70 is no longer locked in a single conformation and switches freely between gauche- and trans orientations.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on MD simulation observations.

claim: The free switching of F70 between conformations results in increased flexibility for both F70 and Y71 and drives occasional opening of the cap loop in nDsbDox.
source: This results in increased flexibility for both F70 and Y71 and drives occasional opening of the cap loop, which in this oxidation state might facilitate nDsbDox receiving electrons from its partner.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a conclusion about the mechanism of loop opening.

claim: The general architecture of the cap-loop region in β- and γ-proteobacteria is conserved.
source: The observation from sequence alignments that the general architecture of the cap-loop region in β- and γ-proteobacteria is conserved, highlights that our observations in E. coli nDsbD can be generalized for many other bacterial species where reductant provision is driven by DsbD in the cell envelope.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on bioinformatics analysis.

claim: It is the oxidation state of the cysteine pair in nDsbD that acts as a 'switch' controlling the presence or absence of local frustration in its active site.
source: Overall, our results show that it is the oxidation state of the cysteine pair in nDsbD that acts as a 'switch' controlling the presence or absence of local frustration in its active site.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a main conclusion of the study.

claim: This oxidation-state-dependent 'switch' determines the dynamic behavior of the cap loop which translates into optimized protein-protein interaction and biological activity.
source: This oxidation-state-dependent 'switch' determines the dynamic behavior of the cap loop which translates into optimized protein-protein interaction and biological activity.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a conclusion about the functional implications.

claim: Redox-state modulation of local frustration may play a wider role in biomolecular recognition in other pathways involving redox proteins which are ubiquitous in all organisms.
source: We propose that redox-state modulation of local frustration, such as that observed here for nDsbD, may play a wider role in biomolecular recognition in other pathways involving redox proteins which are ubiquitous in all organisms.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a proposal for broader implications.
